decisions.reason: This metro data-centre connectivity offer sits squarely in the firm's core network and data-centre knowledge base, and after several years the firm has likely learned enough from use cases to keep improving and retaining it.

Optical spectrum connectivity strongly matches the firm's fibre assets, engineering capabilities and strategic move toward high-bandwidth software-defined infrastructure, so absorptive capacity makes withdrawal unlikely.

The portal builds on existing voice, software-platform and provisioning know-how and can be absorbed into broader digital service operations, though as a voice-related tool it faces some rationalisation risk.

Carrier pre-selection relies on familiar voice capabilities but is a legacy telephony service with weak fit to the firm's forward-looking infrastructure strategy, so management would likely redeploy resources away from it.

Direct voice network connection remains close enough to the firm's enterprise communications base and support capabilities to be maintained, although it is less strategically attractive than newer cloud- and data-led services.
